title: Serre closure for constructible condensed field module sheaves
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying space is noetherian (every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes). For finite intermediate fields $E\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], put $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,E)$ using [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Put $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ with image in one finite intermediate field. A module sheaf is constructible if it has a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which it is pro-etale locally the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules over the restricted coefficient ring. For $A=E_T^c$ with $E$ finite, or $A=\Omega_T^c$, kernels and cokernels of morphisms of constructible $A$-module sheaves are constructible. In every short exact sequence $0\to M\to P\to N\to0$ of $A$-module sheaves, if $M$ and $N$ are constructible, then $P$ is constructible. These assertions use the stratified local finite presentation condition just specified, without a derived completeness condition.

proof.text: Restriction is the actual source-library functor upperStar(Ab,h).mapMod(R). Its finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation follow from the proved upperStar exactness instances and Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_mapMod / preservesFiniteColimits_mapMod. Additivity, mapBiproduct and PreservesCokernel.iso transport finite presentations. Use the monoidality of the composition comparison from [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. Pull back presentation covers using Scheme.Cover.pullback₁ and compose using bind; [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] give the actual pro-etale base-change framework.

For the finite theorem, lift the small field E to ULift E in the scheme universe and construct the sectionwise ring-sheaf isomorphism by continuous ULift.up/down; transport finite presentations and freeness along its pullback. For closure coefficients, remove extendScalars along the invertible condensedPullbackHom via Mod.extendScalarsIsoComapInv. proof.text: First prove local splitting for any epimorphism q:M→N whose target is finite free over an arbitrary commutative ring object on X_proet. Exactness of the source-library Mod.forget makes q.hom epic. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], the image sieve of a section over X contains a covering. A section at the terminal object defines a morphism from the abelian unit (lifted Z), using integer multiples and sheafification adjunction. Comparison of inverse image with localization restriction converts its local lifts to unit morphisms, then Mod.regularLift converts them to R-linear maps. Restrict the cover index using the proved Precoverage.Small instance for propQCPrecoverage. To lift all n basis sections simultaneously, apply this construction once to biproduct.map(q) and the single regular-module map into the biproduct of N containing every basis vector. The resulting biproduct.desc gives a section after conjugation by the free-target isomorphism. Rank zero is included by the empty biproduct. Finally, on a common free cover a morphism is a finite matrix, so its cokernel is finitely presented by its defining presentation; exact inverse image identifies this cokernel with the restricted global cokernel.

proof.text: For an epimorphism f between locally free modules, refine a common free cover by the local splitting just proved. If s is its section, explicitly construct kernel(f)≅cokernel(f≫s): the inverse is induced by id-f≫s, and the universal properties of kernel and cokernel prove the two inverse identities. This cokernel has a finite presentation because source and target are finite free. For an arbitrary f, first its cokernel is locally finitely presented by step 4. Apply local triviality on the noetherian base to that globally defined cokernel and use the epimorphism cokernel.π f to prove Abelian.image f=kernel(cokernel.π f) locally finitely presented. Transfer along Abelian.imageIsoImage, trivialize this global image, and apply the same epimorphism argument to factorThruImage f. The proved kernelFactorThruImage identifies its kernel with kernel f. Local triviality is never applied to a covering object.

proof.text: For a short exact complex Q, take a common cover making Q.X₁ and Q.X₃ finite free, then use step 4 on the restricted epimorphism Q.g and compose the covers. Exact inverse image preserves short exactness. ShortComplex.Splitting.ofExactOfSection identifies the restricted Q.X₂ with the biproduct of the outer terms. Construct the isomorphism finiteFree(m)⊞finiteFree(n)≅finiteFree(m+n) using Fin.castAdd, Fin.natAdd and Fin.addCases. A finite free module is finitely presented as the cokernel of the zero endomorphism. Thus the globally defined Q.X₂ is locally finitely presented. Empty ranks require no separate hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply the locally finitely presented Serre argument on each stratum of the common refinement. PreservesKernel.iso and PreservesCokernel.iso identify the restrictions of global kernels and cokernels with the local constructions; ShortExact.map_of_exact handles extensions. Witness constructibility by this same finite stratification. The two stated theorems are then obtained by specializing the single proved coefficient-ring argument to continuous finite-field coefficients and to bounded-image algebraic-closure coefficients. This proves exactly both original Lean signatures, with no new hypotheses, no new axioms and no new sorry declarations.
